x: Penny was next, followed by Carter, Cohen, Ring, and Wood (who won the Surrey Junior Race the week after) in the first twenty places. Our hopes of repeating our win of last year were now very bright; and we next saw the field coming round Tattenham Corner led by Bert Footer.

Although last, he ran a personal best 51.9 and was given more publicity than the winner Cohen. Charles Elliott announced that Alan had been on duty at the Trooping the Colour all morning and had just made the final---such is fame!
"A Southern Counties 6-Stage Relay was held from Belgrave Hall on April 4th over a four and three-quarter miles lap. Belgrave were winners with Marchant, Patience, Shields, Penny, Cohen and Carter.

On April 29th 1944 Etienne (immediately becoming known as Steve) was elected a member of Belgrave Harriers and he found himself running alongside such notables as Carter, Cohen, Shields and Doubleday.
